entries.title: compacting a session no longer waits on a large index's landmarks
entries.summary: Before Claude Code compacts a conversation, jCodeMunch's PreCompact hook builds a Structural Landmarks section, and Claude Code waits for it. That section loaded and ranked every index holding a file the session touched, with no size cap or time limit. It now uses the same limits as the agent briefing (indexes over 100,000 symbols or of unknown size are skipped, and no index is started after 3 seconds), and it lists any index it skipped and why.

entries.title: a spawned agent no longer waits minutes for its jCodeMunch briefing
entries.summary: The SubagentStart hook briefed every index whose folder overlapped the agent's, and every index on the machine when nothing matched, loading and ranking each one before the agent could start; one report measured a 90-second median and 533 seconds at worst. It now loads at most one index (the most specific one containing the agent's folder, and only if it is small), describes everything else from counts it already has, briefs no repo when nothing matches, and stops ranking after 3 seconds. Reported by treyecollins (#1139).

entries.title: install-pack's licence lookup writes no config file
entries.summary: install-pack without --license looked up your licence key in a way that could create a default config.jsonc when none existed, and that file could pin a new user to the full tool surface. The lookup now reads the config without ever writing one; --license, JCODEMUNCH_LICENSE_KEY and a license_key in config.jsonc resolve as before.

entries.title: a text search earns no savings credit
entries.summary: Your receipt and live savings meter now read lower: search_text and check_references earn no savings credit in either model, because their answer is the matching lines, which Grep returns too, and no measurement supports a credit. The receipt's total is renamed Modeled gross savings. Also: index_file excludes what the full index excludes, listing indexes never writes to other files, the Windows watcher keeps running on battery, and an opted-in git blame no longer goes missing on a busy machine.
